children: Shares of oil marketing companies, aviation firms, paint manufacturers and tyre makers fell by around 1-5 percent on Thursday, as crude oil prices surged amid renewed concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East. Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), IndiGo, Kansai Nerolac Paints and Asian Paints were among the prominent losers as Brent crude climbed above $102 a barrel.

HPCL shares declined 4.7 percent to Rs 327.2, while BPCL fell 4 percent to Rs 284.6. Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) slipped 2.8 percent to Rs 126.4. Aviation major InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo) lost 3.6 percent to trade at Rs 4,812.8.

Paint stocks also came under selling pressure, with Kansai Nerolac Paints falling 4.8 percent to Rs 183.2, Asian Paints declining 1.4 percent to Rs 2,338.8 and JSW Dulux (Akzo Nobel India) down 1.3 percent at Rs 2,989. Berger Paints bucked the trend, rising 0.8 percent to Rs 467.8.

Among tyre manufacturers, CEAT fell 1.4 percent to Rs 3,254.9, Apollo Tyres declined 1.3 percent to Rs 402.3, JK Tyre slipped 1.1 percent to Rs 329.9 and MRF lost 0.6 percent to Rs 122,400. Upstream oil producers also traded lower despite the rise in crude prices. Oil India declined 1.6 percent to Rs 446.7, while ONGC fell 1 percent to Rs 219.8.
Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Updates
Brent crude futures rose $2.28, or 2.28 percent, to $102.28 a barrel by 0427 GMT on Thursday, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures gained $1.66, or 1.88 percent, to $89.94.

Oil prices climbed amid persistent concerns over supplies from the Middle East following an increase in attacks on shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz. Production disruptions in the US, where a hurricane threatened offshore oil facilities, added to supply concerns.

The Strait of Hormuz, which accounted for shipments equivalent to around 20 percent of global oil and fuel supplies before the Iran war, has faced increased threats to shipping in October as the US-Israeli conflict with Iran enters its eighth month.

Crude prices had settled lower on Wednesday after the International Energy Agency agreed to accelerate the release of oil stocks and prioritise diesel supplies under a plan launched in March to address record fuel prices and supply disruptions.

The weakness in oil-linked stocks came amid a broader selloff in Indian equities, tracking declines across Asian markets. At 12:35 pm, the Sensex was down 850 points, or 1.2 percent, at 71,788.5, while the Nifty 50 declined 303 points to 22,300. The Nifty Energy index fell 2.3 percent, while the Nifty Oil & Gas index declined 2.1 percent.

Asian markets also weakened amid concerns over sovereign bond markets and reports of major technology companies seeking to raise billions in debt, adding to competition for funding. Renewed gains in oil prices compounded pressure on US Treasuries, despite a strong auction of 10-year government debt overnight.

title: Oil-sensitive stocks tumble up to 5% as crude prices surge; HPCL, BPCL, IndiGo, Asian Paints fall
